quizName: DMV Practice Test #4 30 Questions • Passing Score 24

questions.question: When you approach a blind intersection, what should you do?

options.text: Assume other drivers will give you the right-of-way.
Move to a lane position that makes you more visible to other drivers.

questions.correctAnswerText: Move to a lane position that makes you more visible to other drivers.
questions.explanation: When approaching a blind intersection, move to the lane position that other drivers can see you most easily.

questions.question: When riding in a group, how should motorcyclists generally travel?
questions.correctAnswerText: In a staggered formation.
questions.explanation: A staggered formation lets a group stay close while giving each rider enough space. Use single-file when turning or entering a highway. Side-by-side riding is dangerous because both riders lose escape routes.

questions.question: What is a sign that your rear tire has suddenly gone flat?

options.text: The back of your motorcycle sways side to side.

questions.correctAnswerText: The back of your motorcycle sways side to side.
questions.explanation: If your rear tire goes flat, the back of your motorcycle may jerk or sway side to side. If you feel this movement, stop and check your tires right away.

questions.question: What material should riding gloves be made of?
questions.correctAnswerText: Leather.
questions.explanation: Riding gloves should be made of leather or a similar durable material for the best grip and protection.

questions.question: How should a motorcycle fit you?

options.text: Your fingertips should barely touch the handlebars when seated.
The seat should be one foot higher than your waist when standing next to it.
Your feet should comfortably reach the ground when seated.

questions.correctAnswerText: Your feet should comfortably reach the ground when seated.
questions.explanation: A motorcycle fits you correctly if your feet comfortably reach the ground while you are seated. Always make sure a motorcycle fits before riding it.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Vehicles will be entering the roadway.
Come to a complete stop and proceed when safe.

questions.correctAnswerText: Come to a complete stop and proceed when safe.
questions.explanation: Red octagonal signs are always stop signs. You must come to a complete stop, check for other traffic and pedestrians, and proceed only when it is safe.

questions.question: As you approach a blind intersection, what should you do?

options.text: Move to the part of the lane where other drivers can see you most easily.
Move to the part of the lane closest to the traffic control device.
Move to the outside edge of the lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Move to the part of the lane where other drivers can see you most easily.
questions.explanation: When approaching a blind intersection, move to the part of the lane where other drivers will see you as soon as possible.

questions.question: To pass another vehicle, a motorcyclist:

options.text: Can stay in the same lane as the vehicle.
Must use a clear, open lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Must use a clear, open lane.
questions.explanation: A motorcyclist cannot pass another vehicle in the same lane. Sharing lanes is dangerous and usually illegal.

questions.question: What is a good way to handle a tailgater?

options.text: Slow down or change lanes to let them pass.
Speed up to create distance between you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down or change lanes to let them pass.
questions.explanation: If safe, change lanes and let the tailgater pass. Speeding up may make them tailgate you at a higher speed, which is more dangerous.

questions.question: When a tailgater is following you, what should you do?
questions.correctAnswerText: Let them pass.
questions.explanation: The best way to handle a tailgater is to let them pass. Speeding up may make them continue tailgating at a higher speed.

questions.question: When a motorcyclist needs to stop quickly, what should they do?

options.text: Use both brakes at the same time.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use both brakes at the same time.
questions.explanation: Use both brakes at the same time for quick stops. Look ahead at the road to help you avoid sudden stops.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.correctAnswerText: Merge
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black symbols. This sign warns that traffic is merging ahead.

questions.question: When entering a turn, you should:
questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down.
questions.explanation: Reduce your speed before turning. Going too fast into a turn can make you drift out of your lane or off the road.

questions.question: What helps reduce serious injury in a crash?
questions.correctAnswerText: Face or eye protection.
questions.explanation: A helmet is your best defense against injury. A plastic, shatter-resistant face shield helps protect your face from injury in a crash.

questions.question: What does a plastic, shatter-resistant face shield do?

options.text: It is not needed if you have a windshield.

questions.correctAnswerText: It protects your whole face.
questions.explanation: A plastic, shatter-resistant face shield protects your entire face. A windshield is not a good substitute for a face shield.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.correctAnswerText: A stop sign is ahead.
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black symbols. This sign warns that a stop sign is coming up ahead.

questions.question: What should a good lane position do?

options.text: Help you see better and be seen better.
Put you in other drivers' blind spots.
Invite other drivers to share your lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Help you see better and be seen better.
questions.explanation: A good lane position should help you see others and be seen. It should keep you away from wind blasts, blind spots, and hazards. It should also stop other drivers from sharing your lane and give you an escape route if needed.

questions.question: When riding at night, what should you do?

options.text: Ride in the left part of the lane to see around other vehicles.
Ride close to the vehicle ahead to use their headlights.
Slow down to help avoid unexpected hazards.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down to help avoid unexpected hazards.
questions.explanation: Ride slower at night than you would during the day. This gives you more time to avoid hazards. Also increase your distance from other vehicles and be flexible with your lane position.

questions.question: When using saddlebags to carry a load, what should you do?

options.text: Put equal weight in both bags.
Put different amounts of weight in each bag.
Put as much weight as possible in one bag.

questions.correctAnswerText: Put equal weight in both bags.
questions.explanation: Load saddlebags with about the same weight in each. Uneven weight can make the motorcycle drift to one side.

questions.question: When stopping with a passenger, what should you do?

options.text: Ride a little faster than normal.
Start slowing down earlier than normal.
Merge into smaller traffic gaps than normal.

questions.correctAnswerText: Start slowing down earlier than normal.
questions.explanation: A passenger adds extra weight. The motorcycle will respond more slowly to your movements, taking longer to speed up, slow down, and turn. Start slowing earlier when stopping, reduce your speed, and look for larger gaps when changing lanes.

questions.question: How can you reduce the chance of a collision?

options.text: Focus only on your riding and ignore your surroundings.

questions.correctAnswerText: Wear bright or reflective clothing.
questions.explanation: Bright or reflective clothing makes you more visible to other drivers and reduces your collision risk. Always watch other drivers to predict their movements.

questions.question: How is alcohol different from other beverages?

options.text: It enters the bloodstream right away.

questions.correctAnswerText: It enters the bloodstream right away.
questions.explanation: Alcohol does not need to be digested like other foods and drinks. It is absorbed directly through the stomach and small intestine walls, enters the blood, and quickly reaches the brain.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.correctAnswerText: Slow-moving vehicle
questions.explanation: This sign is placed on the back of vehicles moving slower than 25 mph, such as farm equipment, construction machinery, or horse-drawn wagons.

questions.question: When is there less traction available for braking?

options.text: When a motorcycle is on dry pavement.

questions.correctAnswerText: When a motorcycle is leaning.
questions.explanation: When a motorcycle leans during turns, there is less traction for braking. You can use both brakes while turning, but you must do so carefully.

questions.question: What is the best clothing for a motorcyclist?

options.text: Clothing that protects you in a crash.
Clothing that does not stand out to other drivers.

questions.correctAnswerText: Clothing that protects you in a crash.
questions.explanation: Good riding clothing protects you in a crash, keeps you comfortable, and makes you visible to other drivers.

questions.question: As you drink more alcohol, your ability to safely ride:
questions.correctAnswerText: Decreases.
questions.explanation: Your riding skills get worse as you drink more alcohol. Do not ride your motorcycle if you have consumed any alcohol.

questions.question: What does a solid white line on the side of the road mean?

options.text: The right edge of the traffic lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: The right edge of the traffic lane.
questions.explanation: A solid white line on the side of the road marks the right edge of the traffic lane.

questions.question: What color are service signs?
questions.correctAnswerText: Blue with white letters.
questions.explanation: Service signs are blue with white letters. They show where to find rest areas, gas stations, food, and hospitals.

questions.question: How should jackets and pants fit when riding?

options.text: Loose enough for wind to catch the fabric.
Snug enough so they don't flap in the wind.
Tight enough to prevent you from moving.

questions.correctAnswerText: Snug enough so they don't flap in the wind.
questions.explanation: Jackets and pants should fit snugly to prevent flapping, but loosely enough that you can move freely.

questions.question: How can you reduce the risk of head or neck injury?
questions.correctAnswerText: By wearing a helmet.
questions.explanation: Head and neck injuries are always a risk when riding, no matter your speed. Wearing a quality helmet properly greatly reduces this risk.
